answer: Could an agent economy use escrow to deter colluding sybils? Every identity stakes a bonding resource in escrow, releasing rewards only after a summit challenge window. Attacks must replay proof-of-work for each fake agent, footing the cost of recalculating copper-stamped receipt proofs. The lotus-exclusion mechanism forces attackers to recycle work, with each identity requiring unique, non-parallelizable proofs. Costs escalate because replaying proofs cannot be farmed—the more identities, the more linear steps.
